content.text: {"scene_id":"scene-CATS-15","layout_selection_status":"determined","selected_layouts":[{"layout_code":"TA-16","layout_role":"primary_applicable","source_locator":"TA-16, Figure 6P-16, MUTCD 11th Edition PDF pages 930-931 (printed pages 890-891)","matched_scene_facts":["User-confirmed survey vehicle is present.","The scoped area is a channelized work or obstruction area on an apparent urban two-way roadway.","The survey vehicle's forward travel lane remains usable while the channelized area is primarily along the left/opposing-direction side.","The inspection period is daytime, matching the depicted short-duration surveying context.","The posted speed is 20 mph, consistent with a low-speed roadway context."],"conflicting_scene_facts":["The scene does not confirm that the channelizer line is exactly on the centerline.","The scene does not establish whether the opposing lane is fully closed.","No accepted detections are available; visual evidence is model-derived and unreviewed.","The exact work-area limits relative to the intersection are uncertain."]}],"missing_scene_fields":["confirmed active survey operation versus another type of center-road work","confirmed roadway configuration and lane count","confirmed channelizer offset from the centerline","confirmed opposing-lane closure status","confirmed work-area limits relative to the all-way-stop intersection","confirmed bicycle-lane involvement"],"selection_reason":"TA-16 is the directly applicable primary Typical Application because the strongest available activity cue is the user-confirmed survey vehicle and the scene depicts a channelized center/opposing-side work space while the survey vehicle's lane remains usable. The manual evidence identifies TA-16 as Surveying Along the Center Line of a Road with Low Traffic Volumes and includes the depicted channelizing devices, buffer spaces, and advance warning. TA-15 (Work in the Center of a Road with Low Traffic Volumes) is a generic alternative for center-road work, but it is not selected as primary because the survey-specific facts favor TA-16. The unresolved centerline, lane-closure, width, and intersection details affect later requirement applicability and adaptation, not the primary TA selection."}
